# 🛡️ Tines — No-Code Security Automation & SOAR Workflow Engine (2025)

---

## 🔎 What Is Tines?

Tines is a no-code automation platform designed specifically for security operations teams. It functions as a SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response) tool, enabling security analysts to build automated workflows for **incident response, threat intelligence gathering, vulnerability management, and compliance reporting** — all without writing code.

Tines focuses on enabling teams — especially security and IT — to connect their technology stack and automate manual processes through an intuitive, story-based interface. Even analysts with limited programming skills can orchestrate complex workflows, because the platform's drag-and-drop approach makes automation accessible to everyone "regardless of technical skill."

---

## 🏢 Company Background

| Detail | Info |
|---|---|
| **Founded** | 2018 |
| **HQ** | Dublin, Ireland |
| **Employees** | 51–200 |
| **Type** | Private |
| **Website** | [tines.com](https://www.tines.com) |

In February 2025, Tines raised **$125M** for its AI-powered workflow automation platform. In July 2025, Tines hired Heather Planishek as COO and CFO, who previously served as Chief Accounting Officer at Palantir and held finance roles at Hewlett-Packard Enterprise and EY.

---

## ⚙️ How It Works — The "Story" Model

The software enables users to create and manage **"stories"** — connected sequences of agents, deterministic automation, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints — that help streamline tasks such as threat detection, data collection, and identity management.

With Tines, your whole team can build any workflow or process — regardless of complexity — without having to write or manage code. The easy-to-use platform lets you get up and running in minutes, not weeks.

---

## 🚀 Key Features (2025)

### 1. 🎨 No-Code / Low-Code Drag-and-Drop Builder
A drag-and-drop canvas is where you build your workflows — from the simple to the intricate and complex — all without having to write or manage code.

### 2. 🔗 Universal API Integration
Unlike legacy SOAR platforms, Tines is built as an **integrator — not on integrations**. It connects to any API to unlock deeper data and insight sharing across tools, both internal or external. As of 2025/2026, Tines includes over **30 built-in integrations** with security tools (CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Splunk, PagerDuty) and supports custom API connections to any service with a REST API.

### 3. 🤖 AI-Powered Automation
Tines enables teams of all sizes and skill sets to build, run, and monitor their most important workflows. The AI and workflow orchestration platform gives teams the tools to enrich data, add contextualization, and meet users where they are — **natural language, no code, low code, or bring your own code**.

Users can leverage LLMs to build, run, and monitor their most important workflows, or build and distribute agents throughout workflows with the **AI Agent action**.

### 4. 🧠 Workspaces (Chatbot Interface)
Tines provides a chatbot interface called **Workspaces**, which enables users to manually specify what tasks the platform should perform using natural language prompts.

### 5. 🚨 Cases — Incident Response Module
The **Cases** tool helps cybersecurity teams respond to breaches faster. It aggregates data from a company's cybersecurity tools in a centralized interface. A checklist shows the steps administrators should take in response to a breach alert, such as mapping out what systems are affected. Cases also includes an analytics dashboard that displays high-level data about a company's cybersecurity efforts.

### 6. 👥 Human-in-the-Loop Workflows
Instead of automating black-and-white remediation actions, teams can ask the affected user or an analyst for their input first. This can be facilitated through automated Slack messages or chatbots — and automating the rest of the workflow based on their response.

# 🔐 Wiz Cloud Security Graph: Cross-Cloud Risk Prioritization Architecture (2025)

---

## 🧠 What Is the Wiz Security Graph?

From the beginning, everything at Wiz has started with the graph—a unified data model that maps every relationship across code, cloud, and runtime. The Wiz Security Graph gives teams a shared language to see risk clearly, prioritize what matters, and act fast.

Wiz connects code, cloud, and runtime into a single security graph that provides the end-to-end context required to automate risk reduction and threat response, enabling security teams to operate at AI speed.

---

## 🏗️ Core Architectural Components

### 1. **Graph Database Foundation (Amazon Neptune)**

Wiz maps all detected risks and the entire technology stack onto the Wiz Security Graph, which was built from the ground up using Amazon Neptune, a serverless graph database service. As a result, Wiz can model the complexity of cloud environments, using both automated and security controls to identify and prioritize risks based on holistic context.

Wiz scans the entire technology stack without agents and stores a graph of the relevant security metadata in Neptune. The Wiz risk engines traverse the graph and weave together interconnected risk factors in seconds.

The security graph processes **1.2 billion asset relationships daily**, ties these insights together, mapping relationships across cloud assets to trace attack paths and potential blast radius (e.g., from a compromised container to an S3 bucket, via GraphQL queries).

---

### 2. **Agentless API Scanning Layer**

Wiz connects in minutes via API and achieves full coverage across cloud and AI resources across PaaS, virtual machines, containers, serverless functions, agents, models, repositories, and pipelines without disrupting business operations or requiring ongoing maintenance. It scales to any cloud and AI environment with zero impact on resource or workload performance.

Wiz's agentless architecture connects directly via APIs, scanning cloud environments without deploying software agents. This approach ensures complete visibility across diverse resources, including PaaS platforms, virtual machines, containers, and serverless functions, simplifying deployment and maintenance.

---

### 3. **Node-and-Edge Graph Model**

Wiz uses the information it gathers to create a **node-and-edge graph** of your assets and their interconnections. This graph, called the Wiz Security Graph, lets Wiz identify the most toxic risk combinations.

An AI security graph is a graph-based model that maps how AI systems actually operate in the cloud. Instead of analyzing models, infrastructure, identities, or data in isolation, it represents them as interconnected nodes—such as AI models, training pipelines, cloud services, service accounts, and data stores—and the relationships between them, including permissions, data flows, and network exposure.

---

### 4. **Multi-Layer Data Ingestion**

The graph ingests signals from multiple layers simultaneously:

- **Workload scanning** collects metadata of operating systems, apps, packages, secrets, and container files to create a list of vulnerabilities and misconfigurations.
- **Data scanning** scans Cloud Storage, non-OS volumes, tables in Cloud SQL, and collects metadata from sensitive data objects.
- **Identity scanning** uses IAM Recommender to find excessive and unused permissions to create Wiz findings.
- **Threat event ingestion** includes Admin Activity audit logs and Security Command Center findings to add threat events.

---

### 5. **SAST + Code-to-Cloud Pipeline**

Wiz SAST expands Wiz Code into proprietary code analysis, giving teams visibility into vulnerabilities in the code they write and the cloud environments where that code runs. Once scanned, SAST findings flow into the Wiz Security Graph, where they're enriched with runtime workload exposure, data access, identity privileges, and attack path insights.

---

## 🎯 Cross-Cloud Risk Prioritization: How It Works

### **"Toxic Combinations" — The Core Prioritization Engine**

The Security Graph is a contextual engine with complete Code-Cloud-Runtime (CLP) coverage. "Toxic Combinations" is Wiz's risk prioritization approach that finds the real attack paths, not just flat vulnerability lists.

Wiz's system evaluates vulnerabilities in context, factoring in **security impact, business relevance, network exposure, and data sensitivity**. This prioritization ensures teams focus on addressing the most critical risks first.

The concept of "context" in cloud security means prioritization. It's the "so what" that tells you a vulnerability is critical because it's public-facing, has high permissions, and touches sensitive data.

### **Exposure Management (GA in 2025)**

Wiz brings together every risk across any infrastructure to determine whether an exposure is actually exploitable and identifies its true impact on the environment. Exposure Management at Wiz includes both **Wiz Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM)** and **Wiz Attack Surface Management (ASM)** to surface true exposure—the issues that form viable attack paths that threat actors could actually exploit.

Wiz UVM centralizes vulnerability data from all scanners—including third parties—into a single tool for prioritization. It centralizes vulnerability findings from cloud, on-prem, and application environments into the Wiz Security Graph, enriching them with context.

### **Attack Surface Management (ASM)**

Wiz ASM provides a clear, validated, and prioritized view of every external exposure across cloud, AI, on-prem, and SaaS environments. It uniquely combines an outside-in attacker's perspective with deep cloud context to help teams focus on the exploitable risks that truly matter before attackers can find them.

---

## ☁️ Cross-Cloud Scope (AWS, Azure, GCP, OCI, and Beyond)

Wiz Cloud provides agentless scanning of cloud infrastructure—**AWS, Azure, GCP, OCI, and Kubernetes**—to identify misconfigurations, vulnerabilities, secrets, and identity risks (CIEM).

Wiz's Security Graph provides deep cross-cloud correlation, connecting code, identities, data, and runtime into one unified attack path model.

The company uses **hundreds of Neptune clusters** deployed over more than **20 AWS Regions** to support this global scale.

### **SaaS Extension (2025)**

Wiz is bringing its agentless cloud security approach to productivity SaaS, starting with **Microsoft 365**. As cloud and collaboration platforms converge, Wiz unifies security context across infrastructure and SaaS, giving teams a single view of risk.

The new integration surfaces misconfigurations, excessive access, identifies sensitive data and secrets in OneDrive and SharePoint, correlates Purview labels, and flags risky sharing links and permissions—all connecting through the Wiz Security Graph.

---

## 🤖 AI & Runtime Security (2025 Evolution)

Wiz AI Security Posture Management (AI-SPM) builds on the Security Graph by identifying AI-specific risks—such as exposed AI services, over-permissioned service accounts, insecure model storage, or sensitive data accessible to AI pipelines—and correlating them with broader cloud context. This allows teams to understand not just that a risk exists, but whether it creates a realistic attack path.

By integrating runtime detection with posture, identity, and workload context, all stitched together via the Wiz Security Graph, the platform offers a powerful foundation for reducing noise, accelerating response, and driving collaboration between security, cloud, and development teams.

---

## 🔁 The "Horizontal Security" Architecture Model (Wizdom 2025)

The new announcements are logical extensions of the graph, designed to enable what Wiz calls **"Horizontal security"**—a move away from siloed, "Vertical" security teams for Dev, Sec, and Ops toward a shared context plane for all.

Where many other security models are vertically oriented, with a silo per security segment, the **horizontal architecture of the Wiz model is fundamentally different**—a shared context layer spanning all teams.

What emerged at Wizdom 2025 was the pivot from **context-for-prioritization** to **context-as-a-knowledge-layer**—a more fundamental architectural shift.

---

## 📊 Architecture Summary Table

| Layer | Technology / Approach | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Data Store** | Amazon Neptune (graph DB) | Store billions of asset relationships |
| **Scanning** | Agentless API scanning | Full cloud coverage, zero agent overhead |
| **Graph Model** | Node-and-edge (assets + relationships) | Map identities, workloads, data, network |
| **Risk Engine** | Toxic Combinations engine | Identify real attack paths, not just alerts |
| **Prioritization** | UVM + ASM + Attack Path Analysis | Surface only exploitable, high-impact risks |
| **Runtime** | eBPF sensor + Wiz Defend | Real-time threat detection + response |
| **Code Layer** | SAST + Wiz Code (ASPM) | Shift risk left to the IDE and CI/CD pipeline |
| **AI Security** | AI-SPM + AI Security Graph | Secure models, pipelines, agents, MCP servers |
| **SaaS Extension** | M365, Databricks, Cloudflare integrations | Extend graph beyond cloud into SaaS + edge |
| **Output** | Wiz Issues → automated workflows | Trigger alerts and remediation automatically |

---

## 🔑 Key Differentiators vs. Competitors

Traditional security solutions use siloed data sources for vulnerabilities, network exposures, and identities, making it difficult to understand the real risk to the customer environment. For example, vulnerabilities from within an internal network may be lower priority than those from the public internet, but traditional cybersecurity tools ignore such nuances. By viewing security in a contextual risk model, organizations can prioritize critical issues and focus remediation efforts on them.

The actionable context created and stored in the graph enables precise answers to proactively identify, prioritize, remediate, and prevent risks to your business. The precision, speed, and explainability of finding risks simply is not possible without using a graph.
